title: Digital Age ~ CLO6 Launch Event Replay [Continuously Updating] p04 D&J Guangzhou Wei Xin CEO - Michael Speech
description: Didn’t have time to finish watching the live stream? No time to watch it live? No problem! The recorded broadcast of the CLO6 launch event is here~ Come and check it out!
transcript:
Thank you for your invitation. Due to the pandemic and work commitments, I was unable to attend the Shanghai conference. Therefore, I can only share a few things with you here at our company in Guangzhou.

Let me first introduce myself. Our company is called Guangzhou City Satellite Fashion Co., Ltd. We are engaged in the supply chain for fast fashion brands and fast fashion stores in Europe and the United States. We have been in this industry for more than 10 years. I am also a user of Code 3D. I have been learning about 3D for two years and have been officially using it for more than one year. So, I would like to share with you, from a user’s perspective, some of the benefits and values of 3D technology in design development and production. Thank you.

I would like to share three points with you.

The first point is that, in my understanding, digitalization is a trend. It is the first application in our company. Actually, the purpose of using 3D is very simple: I want to upgrade this industry. Especially, we can adapt to some changes in the purchasing market. This can improve our company’s competitiveness amid new industrial changes. Because now, the purchasing market demands more from us as suppliers, and the professional level is increasing every year. When we use 3D technology, or digitalization, to upgrade our company, the main purpose is to meet the current requirements of the purchasing market. This way, our customers will have higher annual revenues, and we can serve them well, thereby improving our competitiveness in this industry.

So, more than a year ago, we started cooperating with Code 3D. Of course, until now, the application covers only part of the process. I would like to share with you the application of Code 3D in our company. Actually, I use it in three areas.

First, it is used by a relatively small number of people in marketing and e-commerce products on the internet. I use it to display products on platforms.

The other two uses are for applying 3D technology in OEM and ODM.

I will talk about these three aspects first.

Now, there are preliminary results. Because regarding 3D applications, there are still many scenarios where it can be applied and many functions that can be produced. During implementation, we invested a lot of effort to learn and train more people who can master this technology and use 3D software proficiently together. Simply put, although it has taken a little more than a year, some results have been achieved. Let me briefly introduce them.

For example, in our new product development for Samsung, because I now handle several channels—OEM, ODM—and also have some of my own brand e-commerce channels for promotion, it is very clear that the time spent on designing and developing new products has been greatly improved in efficiency. It also brings some cost reduction and improves the efficiency of our development. Although the time spent on this is relatively short, it indeed brings improvements in various aspects thanks to 3D technology.

Thank you very much. I am grateful to have this opportunity with Code 3D.

I will focus on one example. Because I now have multiple platforms—e-commerce platforms and some internet marketing—I use 3D virtual design for marketing and promotion. I will talk about the Alibaba platform. I also listed some products that I just began using 3D virtual design for marketing and promotion starting in April. I pulled some data from April to September.

In fact, this year, especially in the context of the epidemic, as you can see, in the past six months, by using 3D virtual design for marketing and promotion, we have achieved several times growth. From the peak between April and September, in September and October, we became the leading business on the Alibaba platform in the field of customized women's clothing.

Moreover, in terms of our overall performance, in the whole company, despite our Chinese supply chain system not having fully recovered before May, after recovery in May and June, our sales performance nearly doubled. So, digital upgrades bring us very tangible and immediately visible effects.

We can say that we have achieved very real and immediate results.

However, very few people use virtual 3D in internet marketing or on e-commerce platforms. Perhaps more businessmen or users use it only in actual development and related fields. So, I want to use myself as a case example to show its use in sales and e-commerce product display.

In fact, the effect it brings to our normal, traditional operations is more traffic, more clicks, and even conversions into orders.

I may have mentioned this Code 3D software in our company before, but in fact, we are the first company to use virtual 3D in internet marketing and e-commerce platforms.

We are a European and American brand fast-fashion supply chain company. We are deeply involved in clothing design and development. We are also a supplier of bulk goods, from design to production to delivery. We provide applications for the entire supply chain.

So, I will briefly share my understanding of design and development in OEM.

In the past, when a customer gave us a design or a picture, we had to match the fabric with a material sample. Normally, this took 10 days. But now, we can communicate with customers in two days because when we find the sample in 3D, the customer can immediately see whether it’s the desired result.

Secondly, if we show the sample to the customer, we can share it online wherever they are. Our customers are from Europe, America, and China. Previously, we had to make samples and send them by express delivery. Then we sent them back and forth, paying not only shipping costs but also handling two or three revisions to meet the customer’s real needs.

Now, we can communicate online with the customer. Normally, we gain great benefits from this. The most obvious benefit is cost reduction, especially in international shipping fees. I have reduced fees by 100,000 to 200,000 RMB per month.

Then, due to reducing the need for two or three sample revisions, the cost is greatly decreased. I believe a 50% reduction in cost is conservative; it could be even higher.

This is especially important for international trade. As a cross-border supply chain company, 3D allows for highly efficient coordination anytime, breaking the constraints of time and space. This was unimaginable in the past.

So, I would say digital transformation really helps us increase efficiency.

As a development and production company, we have high demands from our customers. We need to offer the most suitable models for their development, and also provide more ODM models for their design.

In one month, we may have to develop 100 or 200 physical samples for a client, then send them or ask the client to come to select them. But now, I can select samples in advance for a long period, for example, one or two months, using 3D methods to pre-select physical samples for clients.

After the client selects, we make changes based on their feedback and then communicate online. Only after approval do we make a physical sample. This greatly reduces development costs and, more importantly, increases the productivity rate of physical samples.

I can use it for a long time. For example, in the picture below, we have 27 hours of practice. Of course, we may not be able to do that now, but I can do a 2-day practice. The productivity rate is over 55%, increasing by about 2 to 3 times.

So, in terms of development, design, and sample connection, it indeed benefits those of us working in this field by bringing real advantages.

Next, I will briefly discuss 3D technology in our production. My understanding here is shallow. I am currently using it because we have our PLM system and other production systems in ERP.

In terms of Code 3D, it can directly display a sample after modification and also divide the process. As we often say, it has an automatic bumping function.

Traditionally, the flow from clothing development to production is very inefficient. It depends on people and physical sample printing, then sending to the workshop.

Now, with 3D, I can directly communicate with the workshop. For example, in the boardroom or in production communication, 3D can bring similar benefits. We directly provide some produced samples to the workshop and apply them to production.

So, for our entire chain, this is an upgrade in production. I think 3D is a very important middle link.

Previously, for example, the styles we made, including fabric databases and paper samples, in a traditional self-made enterprise, did not have very good reuse or even a second or third use.

Using 3D now, in the early development stages, we have already digitized certain elements, including fabric attributes and fabric scans for classification, the style, platform, paper samples, and so on. This allows division and sharing in our database.

During production, when we need to retrieve information from the database, we can get immediate and effective results, which reduces the cost of many secondary developments.

Also, it modernizes the production process, improving efficiency.

More importantly, it accumulates the data wealth of our company. Previously, such data wealth might be forgotten or discarded within six months. This is the overall value of 3D in production.

Since my time is limited, I will simply share my understanding.

In my view, the upgrade and transformation through 3D is a necessary path. I have only used part of it and have not yet reached the next level, which is very mature.

But it can be said that in the production chain, communication and writing efficiency have really improved significantly and intuitively. It is a very efficient transformation that we can truly feel.

Regarding using virtual reality to replace physical reality, I think it is very good.

Thank you.

Yes, thank you very much.

I think it is threefold. It has a very obvious improvement in our efficiency and cost.

First, I think it is enough to handle our clients.

The quality of the paint or the dyeing result in 3D has already reached the best dyeing result. In fact, I have compared many places. It can accurately show the effect of physical dyeing, at least close to 80% or 90% similarity.

In this regard, even physical dyeing cannot always achieve such effects because results vary. Photography on a 2D screen and 3D display are different.

Then, communication between us and brands or some e-commerce users, including pattern boards and pattern modifications, is very timely and has a very fast response speed.

Because of online modification, after modification, we only proceed to produce the physical dyeing. This is a very fast process and can compress many costs.

Lastly, maybe a simple understanding because I am a partner of some European and American local brands.

For cross-region and cross-country enterprises like ours, I calculated that 3D has reduced costs by about 100,000 to 300,000 RMB monthly and saved time.

Although I have not used it for a long time, for me, the improvements in development, customer communication, marketing, and production are very timely and obvious.

Of course, I hope to become more familiar with it later. With the continuous upgrade of Code 3D, it can be better applied at the production end and will play a greater role there.

Thank you, everyone.

Because my time today is limited, I will stop here.

Thank you.

Michael, please don’t leave the connection yet.

Everyone, Michael, please stay connected. If anyone has questions for Michael, please raise your hands.

Sure.

Okay.

Hello, I have a question.

You talked about recommending some brands to customers. How did you decide to use this 3D software?

I can’t hear you very clearly.

Can you hear me clearly?

Yes, I can.

I want to ask, have you recommended any brands to your customers?

Can you hear me?

Yes, I can.

Regarding the recommended styles, I want to ask how you decided to use this 3D software to recommend. How did you transition from 2D, which is physical clothing, to 3D?

Hello, hello.

Can you hear me clearly?

How did you resolve transitioning from 2D physical clothing to 3D?

I can’t hear you very clearly.

Can you hear me clearly?

Yes, very clear.

So, I want to ask, when you recommended a new style to your customers, did you use this 3D software to recommend? How do you handle the transition from physical clothing to 3D fashion? How do you solve the problem of changing clothing from physical form to a picture?

There are two ways to solve this problem.

The first way is to make a 3D virtual suit for the customer.

We show the product to the customer via the call set.

We also created a cloud platform called SaaS, which allows customers to cooperate with us more effectively.

They can upload our pictures and virtual suits to the cloud platform, and customers can see them directly.

After they make a choice, many customers need modifications.

The next day, we make those changes on the 3D software and send the business team to communicate with them.

This may involve the second and third rounds of changes.

For example, some customers may not use 3D software. Did they have any problems when you recommended the picture at the beginning?

Yes, they did.

How did you solve this problem?

First of all, it is about their adaptability.

During promotion, many customers initially find it unfamiliar.

But as a consistent customer, I convince them that this can help them and improve our supply chain efficiency.

Second, we start to try it.

Because Code 3D’s rendering technology is relatively mature.

If we make a sample from 3D, it can be very close to the physical sample, like a physical sample with 8 or 9 layers.

However, there are slight differences from real physical samples, including texture and the fabric look.

So, we show the fabric picture to the customer.

If they are still uneasy, we send a physical sample.

But, after all, it is enough to send it once.

For example, I do not need to send 100 samples.

If they have problems, I will send it.

That’s it.

Thank you.

I have another question.

You mentioned that after using 3D software, you improved the production rate of samples.

Is this major improvement because you can modify in time or because you can recommend more samples in a short time, increasing your production rate?

It is the first one.

Because we have more designs, maybe some design drafts or pictures, plus some 3D parts.

3D development still takes some time.

In terms of quantity, the fastest is that we may have collected many design drafts and pictures.

What I mean by increased production rate refers to the number of physical samples.

Previously, we made physical samples for clients to choose.

Now, for example, if the 3D picture is not OK, I reject it.

If it needs changes, I change it immediately.

If the customer agrees, we then make the physical sample.

So, I think it is a good approach.

Therefore, the usage rate of physical samples is higher.

Okay.

Thank you.

Can I end the questions here?

Yes, you can.

Thank you.

Do you have any other questions?

If not, we would like to thank Michael for his speech today.

Thank you, Michael.

Thank you.

chunks.content: # Digital Age ~ CLO6 Launch Event Replay ## Speech by Michael, CEO of Guangzhou City Satellite Fashion Co., Ltd. This document presents a detailed user perspective on the application of 3D technology (Code 3D) in fast fashion supply chain processes, highlighting benefits in design development, marketing, OEM/ODM production, cost reduction, and efficiency improvements. --- ## Introduction to Company and 3D Technology Adoption Michael is the CEO of Guangzhou City Satellite Fashion Co., Ltd., a supply chain company serving fast fashion brands and stores in Europe and the U.S. with over 10 years of industry experience. He has been using Code 3D technology for over a year after two years of learning. The company aims to upgrade its processes through digitalization, particularly leveraging 3D technology to meet evolving purchasing market demands and enhance competitiveness. --- ## Strategic Purpose of 3D Technology in the Supply Chain This section covers the motivation behind adopting 3D technology, focusing on digital transformation to adapt to changing market requirements and improve company competitiveness. - **Digitalization as a Trend:** The company views digital transformation as essential to respond to increasing professional and market demands. - **Goals:** Improve customer revenue, enhance service quality, and elevate competitive standing through 3D. - **Scope of Application:** Currently applied in parts of the process, primarily in marketing, e-commerce product display, and OEM/ODM development. --- ## Application Areas of Code 3D in the Company Michael identifies three main areas where Code 3D is used: 1. **Marketing and E-commerce:** Displaying products virtually on internet platforms to boost engagement and sales. 2. **OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer):** Assisting in design development and client communication. 3. **ODM (Original Design Manufacturer):** Supporting design innovation and sample selection. --- ## Marketing and Sales Impact Using 3D Virtual Design This section details how 3D virtual design has enhanced marketing efficiency and sales performance. - The company began utilizing 3D virtual designs on e-commerce platforms like Alibaba starting April. - Between April and September, there was several-fold growth in marketing effectiveness during the COVID-19 pandemic. - By September and October, the company became a leading seller of customized women's clothing on Alibaba. - Post-pandemic supply chain recovery led to nearly doubled sales, attributable in part to digital upgrades. - 3D marketing applications increase traffic, clicks, and conversion rates. - The company was among the first to apply virtual 3D in internet marketing and e-commerce. --- ## Enhancements in Design and Development Through 3D Technology This section explains how 3D technology has transformed the design and product development cycle, especially in OEM operations. - **Faster Sample Matching:** Previously, matching fabric samples to designs took about 10 days; now it takes about 2 days with 3D visualization. - **Remote Client Communication:** Samples are shared online globally, eliminating multiple physical shipments and reducing shipping and revision costs. - **Cost Reduction:** Monthly savings on international shipping fees range from 100,000 to 200,000 RMB. - **Sample Revision Efficiency:** Reduces the need for 2-3 physical sample iterations, potentially cutting costs by at least 50%.

Creating 3D virtual suits to present to customers via video calls. 2. Using a proprietary cloud-based SaaS platform where customers can view and collaborate on virtual samples. - Customers upload images and virtual suits to the cloud for selection. - Iterative modifications are performed in 3D software and communicated by the business team. - Initial customer resistance due to unfamiliarity is addressed through education and demonstration of supply chain efficiency benefits. - Code 3D’s mature rendering technology produces samples close to physical quality (8-9 layer texture fidelity). - Physical samples are still sent when customers are uneasy, but typically only once, avoiding multiple shipments. --- ## Improvements in Sample Production Rates Michael explains how 3D technology has increased the efficiency and utilization of physical samples. - The main driver is timely modification and approval enabled by 3D visualization. - Design drafts and 3D components speed up internal development. - Physical samples are only produced after customer approval of 3D renderings. - This approach increases the usage rate of physical samples and reduces waste. - The company can reject or modify virtual samples quickly before physical production, optimizing resources. --- # Summary Michael’s speech illustrates the transformative role of 3D technology (Code 3D) in the fast fashion supply chain, from design and marketing to production. Key benefits include accelerated development cycles, significant cost savings (up to hundreds of thousands of RMB monthly), enhanced customer communication, and increased sample productivity. The technology bridges geographic and temporal gaps in international trade, modernizes workflows, and builds valuable digital assets for the company. Challenges in customer adaptation to virtual samples are addressed via cloud platforms and education. Continuous software upgrades promise even greater future impact. --- # Glossary - **Code 3D:** A 3D virtual design software used for product visualization and development. - **OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer):** Company producing products based on designs provided by another company. - **ODM (Original Design Manufacturer):** Company designing and producing products that are eventually branded by another firm. - **PLM (Product Lifecycle Management):** System to manage product development processes. - **ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning):** Integrated system to manage business processes, including production. - **SaaS (Software as a Service):** Cloud-based software delivery model. - **Bump Mapping:** A 3D graphics technique to simulate texture and surface detail. --- # Key Metrics and Figures - 10+ years in fast fashion supply chain. - 2 years learning 3D, 1+ year active use of Code 3D. - 100-200 physical samples developed monthly per client. - 50%+ reduction in sample revision costs. - 100,000 to 300,000 RMB monthly cost savings. - 27 hours of 3D practice training reported.
